designVerdict: SELECTED - FOUR per board: Q3/Q4 channel enable (one per channel), Q5/Q6 FAULT interlock (one per channel). All four switch a low-voltage divider node, not a 36 V gate.
notes: Each device pulls one LM5069 UVLO pin below 2.5 V. Q3/Q4 carry a 100 kOhm gate pull-up to 3V3 so the channels are off through MCU reset, and firmware drives the GPIO LOW to enable - the inverted sense is the fail-safe direction.

THE FAULT INTERLOCK NEEDS TWO DEVICES, NOT ONE. A MOSFET drain is a single node, so one device tied to both UVLO pins would short the two dividers together and each enable transistor would then disable both channels, destroying independent per-channel shedding.

GATE DRIVE IS MARGINAL on Q5/Q6. HUSB238A FAULT/OUT2 is push-pull at Voh >= 0.8 x VDD (p.8) = 2.64 V on a 3.3 V rail, against this part's Vgs(th) 2.5 V MAX at 250 uA - about 0.14 V of worst-case overdrive to sink the ~97 uA needed. A logic-level MOSFET would remove the question. Q3/Q4 driven from a 3.3 V GPIO are fine.
SUPERSEDED: earlier notes here described level-shifting a 36 V P-FET gate off the HUSB238A GATE pin, and gave a count of three. Neither is the circuit; that topology does not exist in the design.
